What You Need defaults to required; Bonus Points is optional. Required mentions of RAG, prompt engineering, orchestration, and LangChain override their bonus mentions.
SQL, PQL, and Celonis coding appear as skills to be taught, not candidate prerequisites; technologies appearing only in role descriptions or responsibilities are excluded.
Read prompt/context engineering literally as naming both prompt engineering and context engineering; the latter has no taxonomy entry.
Multi-agent orchestration maps to LLM orchestration; whether it additionally names multi-agent systems is flagged for review.
Common ML libraries is treated as a tool category, not a separate request for the parent skill machine learning. Its concrete examples are included.
Intelligent chatbots and automated text processors are described as use-case examples, not separate candidate skills.
Oracle is left unmapped rather than interpreted as a specific database product because the posting identifies it as an ERP example.
Proof-of-concept work and ROI/TCO modeling are treated literally as technical practices without matching taxonomy entries; these and the ERP entries occur under Bonus Points and are optional.
Degree fields, business acumen, supply-chain knowledge, sales experience, and soft skills are excluded from skills under the guide.
